title: Covered glass pedestrian bridge spanning between buildings with rooftop installations
objects_and_counts: No people are visible in the photographed scene.

One large curved glass atrium / covered walkway is visible occupying the center-left to center of the image; the glass enclosure is made of multiple repeated rectangular window panels held in a white frame.
One enclosed pedestrian bridge (walkway) runs from lower left to upper right across the image, passing through the glass enclosure and continuing to the adjacent building on the right.
One multi-storey building with many horizontal rows of windows is visible on the right side of the image; individual window openings are repeated across at least five visible floors.

At least three rooftop installations or sculptural devices are visible on the roof of the right-hand building, aligned roughly along the roof edge; the exact type of these devices is not identified by visible labels.
At least two trees are visible beneath the bridge in the lower central area of the image.

At least one small cluster of orange seating (appears to be two or three seats and possibly a small table) is visible on the lower level beneath the bridge; seating is partially obscured by tree foliage and bridge structure.
One large white sloped structural element (possibly part of an adjacent roof or facade) runs diagonally from lower right toward center of image.
One software watermark/notification graphic is present in the lower-left corner of the image (separate from scene objects).
spatial_relations: The curved glass atrium covers the pedestrian walkway and is located to the left and center of the image; the enclosure follows the curve of the walkway.
The walkway runs diagonally from lower left to upper right, passing through the glass enclosure and connecting to the taller dark-grey building on the right.

The dark-grey building occupies the right third of the image with horizontal bands of windows; rooftop installations are located on top of that building near its edge toward the top-right of the image.
Beneath the bridge and adjacent to the white sloped structural element, trees and a small orange seating area are situated at ground level in the lower central area.
The large white sloped element sits between the glass-covered walkway and the lower ground area, forming an angular plane that casts shadows onto the area beneath the bridge.
colours_and_materials: The glass panels of the atrium appear bluish-tinted with white framing members forming a grid.
The walkway and structural framing are predominantly white or light-coloured.
The adjoining building facade is dark grey or charcoal with contrasting rectangular window openings.
Green foliage is visible from the trees beneath the bridge.
A small seating grouping beneath the bridge is orange in colour.
The watermark/notification graphic in the lower-left corner uses black, white and a gold/orange gem icon.
uncertainties: No room name or room number signage is visible in the image; location cannot be determined from the image alone.
The exact count of rooftop installations is given as 'at least three' because some devices are partially obscured by perspective and distance.
The small orange seating area beneath the bridge is partially obscured by tree foliage and the bridge structure; the precise number of seats and tables cannot be determined.
Small text on distant rooftop elements or window labels, if present, is unreadable at the image resolution.
The function of the white sloped structural element is not identifiable from the visible geometry; it may be a roof, ramp or facade element but that is not confirmed by legible labels.
